office_does: The three county commissioners set Chelan County's budget and pass county ordinances and land-use rules; District 2 candidates are nominated by District 2 voters, and the whole county elects the winner.
race_blurb: First-term Commissioner Shon Smith (prefers Republican), board chair since 2025, faces Leavenworth City Council member Clint Strand (prefers Democrat) after a primary decided by 120 votes. Smith runs on experience and representing rural unincorporated areas. Strand runs on trust in county operations, housing partnerships and ending reserve draws to balance the budget.

candidates.summary: Cashmere restaurant owner elected commissioner in 2022 and board chair since 2025, running for a second term on experience, rural representation and keeping taxes low.
highlights: Says the county must keep 'taxes low while also keeping the roads paved and the bridges in good repair' [S5]
Voted for the 2024 ordinance letting deputies trespass people camping on county property [S12]
Voted in 2023 to strike denser zoning from Leavenworth's growth area, citing rural character; reversed in 2024 after a state board ruling [S10][S11]
Says he is taking no campaign donations and that 'campaign spending is out of control' [S5]
Placed first in the District 2 primary, 4,368 to 4,248 [S7]

experience.basis: Incumbent commissioner and board chair whose campaign is built on 'Chelan County Needs an Experienced Commissioner.'

taxes.basis: Lists 'Responsible taxation' and says the county is 'always concerned about keeping taxes low'; no proposal to cut specific taxes.

spending.basis: States a spend-less-than-you-have goal and backed permit fees that end a general-fund subsidy, but describes planned deficit budgets, and a colleague's balanced-budget goal motions died without his support.

safety.basis: Voted for the encampment trespass ordinance and lists support for the sheriff and first responders; also cites a four-county diversion facility.

reform.basis: Says he refuses campaign donations because spending is 'out of control' and donations misrepresent voter support; PDC mini-reporting registration is consistent with that.

candidates.summary: Leavenworth City Council member since 2017 and Finance Committee chair, executive director of the Wenatchee Valley College Foundation, running on trust in county operations, housing and a balanced budget.
highlights: Says the county 'can't keep dipping into our reserve funds to make the math work' [S1]
Proposes regional partnerships and incentives for builders to create starter and ownership housing [S1][S6]
Calls trust the county's most pressing issue and promises expectations and accountability for county services [S3][S6]

experience.basis: Challenger to the incumbent who promises a new approach to trust and accountability, though he has eight-plus years on a city council.

spending.basis: Criticizes reserve draws and pledges to adjust services so 'our books balance'; no proposals to expand programs.

housing.basis: Housing plan centers on incentives for builders and identifying areas for development to add ownership housing, not public housing or tenant protections.
